financials_interim.notes: Pan Asia Banking Corporation PLC (PABC), a licensed commercial bank (FYE 31 December). Single-entity filing -- no separate Bank/Group columns anywhere in the Income Statement, Statement of Comprehensive Income, Statement of Financial Position, Statement of Changes in Equity, or Statement of Cash Flows; the word 'Group' does not appear anywhere in this filing, the certification page refers only to 'Pan Asia Banking Corporation PLC' and 'the Bank' throughout, and the 'Selected Performance Indicators' page is headed simply 'Bank' with a single column. No subsidiaries are referenced. Entered as a single basis='GROUP' row per this project's convention for single-entity bank/NBFI filings (same treatment as CBNK earlier this session). This entry uses the filing's 6-MONTH CUMULATIVE (H1, six months ended 30 June 2026) figures; the filing also separately gives quarter-only columns (Q2 2026 vs Q2 2025, not used here, though referenced qualitatively in the narrative). Mapped per bank convention: revenue = 'Total Operating Income' (Rs.8,677,955k H1 2026 / Rs.7,931,350k H1 2025); operating_profit = the Bank's own 'Operating Profit before Taxes on Financial Services' subtotal (Rs.3,911,430k / Rs.3,827,119k); profit_before_tax = the Bank's own 'Profit before Tax' line, AFTER the 'Taxes and Levies on Financial Services' deduction (Rs.977,236k H1 2026 / Rs.920,977k H1 2025) -- that levy is not separately stored. finance_costs/finance_income left blank -- interest expense (Rs.11,133,417k) is already netted into revenue via Net Interest Income. current_assets/current_liabilities/inventory/trade_receivables/trade_payables left blank per bank convention (liquidity-ordered balance sheet; Loans and Advances is the core lending book, not a trade receivable). short_term_borrowings = 'Due to Banks' (Rs.14,158,114k); long_term_borrowings = 'Repurchase Agreements' + 'Due to Debt Securities Holders' (Rs.12,181,814k + Rs.16,437,643k = Rs.28,619,457k), per this task's explicit convention that repo with other institutions and debentures/subordinated debt both fall under long_term_borrowings for this entry (note this differs slightly from the NTB entry earlier this session, which treated repo as short-term -- followed the instructions given specifically for this PABC entry). 'Due to Depositors' (Rs.271,238,948k) deliberately excluded from both borrowings fields -- deposit funding, not debt. cash_and_equivalents = Balance Sheet line 'Cash and Cash Equivalents' (Rs.7,327,066k) -- note the Cash Flow Statement's broader 'Cash & Cash Equivalents as per the Statement of Cash Flows' figure (Rs.13,865,096k) additionally includes Placements with Banks and is not used here, for consistency with the balance-sheet-line convention used in prior entries this session. unit_scale='000' confirmed from 'In Rupee Thousands' header on every statement page. shares_in_issue = 442,561,629 (all voting; no non-voting shares exist per the Statement of Changes in Equity footnote and the Shareholders' Information page, where the Market Price table's 'Non-Voting' column is blank) -- Stated Capital was unchanged at Rs.3,614,253k throughout both H1 2025 and H1 2026 (no rights issue, no new share issuance), so period-end count equals the weighted-average count used for EPS. Cross-check: Rs.2,502,057,000 / 442,561,629 shares = Rs.5.6536, rounds to the disclosed EPS of Rs.5.65 exactly -- confirms the share count and no undisclosed share-count change during the period. IMPORTANT FINDING: the Income Tax Expense line fell 42.7% YoY (Rs.754,231k H1 2025 to Rs.432,137k H1 2026, a decline of Rs.322,094k) despite Operating Profit before Taxes on Financial Services being essentially flat (+2.2%, Rs.3,827,119k to Rs.3,911,430k) and PBT growing only 1.0% (Rs.2,906,142k to Rs.2,934,194k). The filing's own narrative explicitly attributes this to 'the reversal of excess income tax provisions relating to prior years' -- i.e. a one-off, non-recurring tax benefit, not an improvement in the underlying effective tax rate on ongoing operations. This Rs.322,094k tax decline accounts for ~92% of the total Rs.350,146k increase in Profit for the Period (PAT +16.3% YoY to Rs.2,502,057k) -- so the headline PAT growth is overwhelmingly a tax-timing effect rather than operating profit growth, similar in kind (if smaller in relative magnitude) to the one-off tax credit found at NTB earlier this session. tax_expense is still stored as a positive value (432137) since it remained a genuine expense, not a credit, in both periods -- unlike NTB where the Group tax line swung to an outright credit. No column-swap issues found -- Total Assets (354,034,099) = Total Liabilities + Equity (322,128,801 + 31,905,299 = 354,034,100, immaterial Rs.1k rounding); PBT - tax_expense = PAT ties exactly (2,934,194 - 432,137 = 2,502,057).

interim_updates.note_text: Pan Asia Bank's Total Operating Income grew 9.4% YoY to Rs.8.68bn for H1 2026 (six months ended 30 June 2026), driven by a 13.0% increase in Net Interest Income to Rs.7.07bn (interest income +21% to Rs.18.21bn, outpacing a 27% rise in interest expense to Rs.11.13bn as deposit and borrowing costs rose industry-wide) and a 27.6% increase in Net Fee and Commission Income to Rs.1.46bn, driven by credit expansion, card usage, trade finance and remittance inflows. Net Interest Margin moderated to 4.29% from 4.55%, mainly on lower returns from the Government Securities portfolio. These gains were largely offset at the trading/treasury line: Net Gains from Trading fell 31% to Rs.171.6mn and Net Gains from Derecognition of FVOCI Financial Assets fell 74% to Rs.66.8mn, both attributed to rising Treasury bill and bond yields reducing mark-to-market and realisation gains -- consistent with the Treasury and Investments segment's result falling to Rs.176.2mn from Rs.1,274.3mn a year earlier (segment note, page 18-19), even as the Retail & SME Banking segment result grew 39% to Rs.4,673.5mn and Corporate Banking grew 33% to Rs.397.9mn. Impairment charges rose 32% YoY to Rs.399.7mn (Stage 1 charge Rs.124.2mn, Stage 2 Rs.278.1mn, Stage 3 Rs.132.9mn) as a deliberate prudential measure, even as asset quality metrics improved: Gross Stage 3 (impaired loan) ratio improved to 3.97% from 4.62% at end-2025, Net Stage 3 ratio to 1.39% from 1.73%, and Stage 3 provision coverage rose to 64.92% from 62.63%. Operating expenses grew 14.9% YoY to Rs.4.37bn (Personnel expenses +16.3% to Rs.2.10bn, Depreciation & Amortisation +11.7% to Rs.327.2mn, Other Operating Expenses +14.0% to Rs.1.94bn), driven by technology and digital transformation investment, pushing the Cost-to-Income Ratio up to 50.32% from 48.94%. As a result, Operating Profit before Taxes on Financial Services was essentially flat YoY (+2.2% to Rs.3.91bn), and after Taxes and Levies on Financial Services (+6.1% to Rs.977.2mn), Profit Before Tax grew just 1.0% to Rs.2.93bn. However, Profit After Tax grew a much larger 16.3% to Rs.2.50bn -- this gap is explained by the Income Tax Expense line falling 42.7% YoY (Rs.754.2mn to Rs.432.1mn, a decline of Rs.322.1mn), which the filing explicitly attributes to 'the reversal of excess income tax provisions relating to prior years'. This one-off tax reversal of Rs.322.1mn accounts for approximately 92% of the total Rs.350.1mn increase in PAT -- underlying pre-tax operating performance was essentially flat, not up 16%. Total Assets crossed Rs.350bn for the first time (+15% YoY to Rs.354.03bn), Gross Loans and Advances grew 14% to Rs.248.13bn, and Customer Deposits grew 17% to Rs.271.24bn. Capital and liquidity remained comfortably above regulatory minimums (CET1/Tier 1 14.93%, Total Capital Ratio 16.47%, Rupee LCR 221.63%, All Currency LCR 168.79%, NSFR 128.96%).
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is the first financial_statements entry for PABC in this database (zero prior rows existed for this symbol before this entry). This entry uses the filing's 6-MONTH CUMULATIVE (H1, six months ended 30 June 2026) figures as the primary stored figures; the filing separately provides quarter-only columns (Q2 2026 vs Q2 2025) which were not used as the stored figures but were referenced qualitatively in the narrative (e.g. Q2 2026 PAT of Rs.1,451.9mn vs Q2 2025's Rs.1,135.1mn, +28%, a faster quarter-only growth rate than the H1 cumulative +16.3%, partly reflecting the timing of the tax provision reversal within the half).
interim_updates.takeaway: The 16.3% PAT growth headline (Rs.2.15bn to Rs.2.50bn) is mostly a tax-timing effect, not operating strength: a Rs.322.1mn reversal of excess prior-year income tax provisions explains roughly 92% of the PAT increase, while Operating Profit before Taxes on Financial Services was essentially flat (+2.2%) and Profit Before Tax grew just 1.0%. The genuine bright spots are core banking growth (NII +13%, net fee income +28%, balance sheet crossing Rs.350bn for the first time, improving Stage 3/NPL ratios) and a conservative +32% increase in impairment provisioning; the drags are a weak Treasury/trading result (segment PBT down from Rs.1,274.3mn to Rs.176.2mn on falling bond/trading gains as yields rose) and a 15% rise in operating expenses that pushed the Cost-to-Income Ratio up to 50.32% from 48.94%.

yoy.label: Operating Profit before Taxes on Financial Services

operational_highlights: Total Operating Income +9.4% YoY to Rs.8.68bn; Net Interest Income +13.0% to Rs.7.07bn; Net Fee and Commission Income +27.6% to Rs.1.46bn

Operating Profit before Taxes on Financial Services essentially flat (+2.2%) at Rs.3.91bn; PBT +1.0% to Rs.2.93bn; but PAT +16.3% to Rs.2.50bn -- the PAT/PBT growth gap is explained almost entirely by a Rs.322.1mn (-42.7%) decline in Income Tax Expense, which the filing attributes to 'the reversal of excess income tax provisions relating to prior years' and which alone explains ~92% of the PAT increase

Treasury and Investments segment result fell to Rs.176.2mn from Rs.1,274.3mn a year earlier (segment note); Net Gains from Trading -31% to Rs.171.6mn and Net Gains from Derecognition of FVOCI -74% to Rs.66.8mn, both attributed to rising Treasury bill/bond yields reducing mark-to-market and realisation gains
Impairment charges +32% YoY to Rs.399.7mn as a deliberate prudential measure, even as Gross Stage 3 ratio improved to 3.97% from 4.62% and Stage 3 coverage rose to 64.92% from 62.63%

Operating expenses +14.9% to Rs.4.37bn (Personnel +16.3% to Rs.2.10bn, driven by headcount growth to 1,644 employees; Depreciation & Amortisation +11.7% on technology/digital investment); Cost-to-Income Ratio rose to 50.32% from 48.94%
Total Assets crossed Rs.350bn for the first time (+15% YoY to Rs.354.03bn); Gross Loans and Advances +14% to Rs.248.13bn; Customer Deposits +17% to Rs.271.24bn
key_drivers: A Rs.322.1mn reversal of excess prior-year income tax provisions (Income Tax Expense -42.7% YoY to Rs.432.1mn) is the single largest driver of the PAT growth headline, explaining ~92% of the Rs.350.1mn increase in Profit for the Period -- a one-off tax-timing benefit, not an operating improvement

NII growth (+13.0% to Rs.7.07bn) and Net Fee and Commission Income growth (+27.6% to Rs.1.46bn) are genuine core-business drivers of revenue growth, per the segment note led by the Retail & SME Banking segment (result +39% to Rs.4,673.5mn) and Corporate Banking (+33% to Rs.397.9mn)

Rising Treasury bill and bond yields during the period reduced mark-to-market and realisation gains on the investment book (Net Gains from Trading -31%, Net Gains from Derecognition of FVOCI -74%), dragging the Treasury and Investments segment result down to Rs.176.2mn from Rs.1,274.3mn -- an external market-yield effect rather than a credit or operating issue

Operating expenses growth of 14.9% (Personnel +16.3%, Depreciation & Amortisation +11.7%) driven by technology, digital transformation and business infrastructure investment pushed the Cost-to-Income Ratio to 50.32% from 48.94%, offsetting revenue growth at the pre-levy operating profit line
